name: Meesho
summary: Candidates commonly report that Meesho's engineering interviews include an online coding test, problem-solving rounds, a low-level design or machine coding round and, for experienced roles, system design, followed by a hiring manager conversation. Meesho's marketplace serves small sellers and value-conscious buyers, many in smaller towns, so questions often turn to those users, regional languages and keeping costs low at scale.
rounds: Online coding test (for many engineering roles)
Low-level design or machine coding round
looks_for: Putting users first: buyers, sellers and delivery partners
Speed: shipping a first version fast and improving it
Acting like an owner of the outcome
Thinking big and long term, not only about the next quarter
Starting from the problem before the solution
Keeping costs low so the product stays affordable

questions.text: Tell me about a time you shipped a first version quickly and improved it based on what users did.
covers: What the first version included and what you left out on purpose
What users' behaviour showed you
The changes you made and the result

questions.text: Describe a time you put your company's or team's goal ahead of your own project.
covers: The conflict between the two
Why you chose the bigger goal and what it cost you
What it achieved for the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you spoke up because you thought a plan was wrong.
covers: What was wrong and how you knew
How you raised it, and with whom
What changed, or what you did if the plan went ahead

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you got wrong. How did you find out, and what did you change?
covers: The decision and why it seemed right then
The signal that showed it was wrong
The fix, and what you now check before deciding

questions.text: How would you design a catalogue upload flow for small sellers who list products from their phones?
covers: A simple mobile flow: photos, a few fields, bulk upload for many items
Checks: image quality, duplicates, banned items, with clear feedback to the seller
Processing in the background, and support for regional languages

questions.text: How would you recommend products to buyers who are new to online shopping and browse in their own language?
covers: Starting with little history: what is popular in their region and category
Learning quickly from views, wishlists and orders
Judging success by orders kept, not only clicks, so returns count against it

questions.text: Returns are high in one clothing category. How would you reduce them without hurting sales?
covers: Finding the reasons from return data: size, quality, product not as pictured
Fixes: better size guides, clearer photos, seller quality scores
Watching return rate, orders and ratings together

questions.text: How would you keep infrastructure costs low for a service with heavy traffic and low-value orders?
covers: Measuring cost per request or per order first
Caching, cheaper storage tiers, right-sized servers, batch jobs at quiet hours
Where you wouldn't save money: reliability of checkout and payments

questions.text: How would you design an API and app to work well on slow mobile networks and low-end phones?
covers: Small responses, pagination and compression
Images sized for the device, and caching on the phone
Safe retries for requests that time out

questions.text: How would you detect sellers listing fake or misleading products across a very large catalogue?
covers: Signals: returns and complaints, copied images, prices far below normal
Automated rules or models first, then human review
Penalties and an appeal process, and the cost of wrongly flagging honest sellers

questions.text: Estimate how many new sellers could be brought onto the platform from one textile hub, such as Surat, in a year.
covers: A clear structure: businesses in the hub, the share ready to sell online, the share you can reach
Limits such as onboarding capacity and seller support
A sanity check on the final number

questions.text: Why Meesho? What do you understand about the buyers and sellers it serves?
covers: Who the buyers and sellers are, in a sentence each
Why building for them interests you
How your skills would help them

questions.text: Are you comfortable building for users whose lives are very different from yours? How would you learn about them?
covers: An honest answer, with an example of learning about unfamiliar users
Methods: talking to users, watching recordings, reading support tickets
How what you learn would change what you build

tips: Keep Meesho's users in mind: buyers watching every rupee and sellers running small businesses. Bring them into design and product answers.
Practise low-level design: clear classes and interfaces and a working demo within the time.
Treat cost as a design constraint; cost per order matters a lot for a marketplace built around low prices.
Use the app as a buyer before the interview, and look at the seller side if you can, so you can talk about real flows.
